q.s: A 35-year-old chef cuts the base of his right palm with a knife. Afterward, he cannot touch the tip of his thumb to the tip of his little finger. Sensation over the thumb and index finger is normal.
o: Palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve
Main trunk of the median nerve at the elbow
Recurrent branch of the median nerve
e: Wrong. Would cause sensory loss and forearm weakness.
Correct. Loss of thenar muscles (opposition) without sensory loss.
q.k: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
cl: cuts the base of his right palm
cannot touch the tip of his thumb to the tip of his little finger
Sensation over the thumb and index finger is normal
q.ch: Superficial thenar laceration + loss of opposition + normal sensation → recurrent branch of median nerve ("ape hand").
q.tr: The recurrent branch is the "million-dollar nerve."
q.q2: Which nerve is most likely injured?

q.s: A 26-year-old man falls on his outstretched hand. He now has tingling in his thumb, index and middle fingers. Lateral wrist x-ray shows that one carpal bone has rotated forward into the palm, out of line with the radius and capitate.
e: Correct. Lunate dislocation can impinge the median nerve in the carpal tunnel.
Wrong. Hook fracture affects the ulnar nerve.
cl: tingling in his thumb, index and middle fingers
rotated forward into the palm, out of line with the radius and capitate
q.ch: FOOSH + median paresthesias + volar carpal dislocation → lunate dislocation → acute carpal tunnel syndrome.
q.tr: Scaphoid fractures; lunate dislocates.
q.q2: Which carpal bone is dislocated?

q.s: A 40-year-old man fell onto his hand while mountain biking and fractured the hook of the hamate 3 months ago. Now, when he extends his fingers, his ring and little fingers are flexed at the interphalangeal joints and hyperextended at the metacarpophalangeal joints. Wrist flexion is normal.
o: Unopposed flexor digitorum profundus (spared in a distal lesion) with loss of the ulnar lumbricals
cl: fractured the hook of the hamate
ring and little fingers are flexed at the interphalangeal joints
q.ch: Hook of hamate fracture → distal ulnar nerve → loss of ulnar lumbricals with intact FDP → ulnar claw on finger extension.
q.tr: The more distal the ulnar lesion, the worse the claw.
q.q2: Why are the interphalangeal joints flexed?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has aching in her left arm when she works with her arms overhead, with tingling along the inner forearm and little finger. The intrinsic hand muscles are wasted. When she raises her arm, her radial pulse weakens and her hand becomes pale. Chest x-ray shows an extra rib arising from C7.
o: Lower trunk of the brachial plexus and subclavian artery
Median nerve at the carpal tunnel
Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex artery
e: Correct. Thoracic outlet syndrome from a cervical rib.
cl: tingling along the inner forearm and little finger
her radial pulse weakens and her hand becomes pale
q.ch: Cervical rib → compression of lower trunk and subclavian artery in the scalene triangle → Klumpke-like hand + vascular signs.
q.tr: Brachial plexus and subclavian artery pass between the anterior and middle scalenes.
q.q2: Which structures are compressed?

q.s: A 29-year-old woman at 36 weeks of pregnancy has burning pain and numbness over the outer front of her right thigh. Strength and reflexes are normal.
e: Wrong. Would cause weakness and reflex loss.
Wrong. Genital and upper medial thigh.
Correct. Meralgia paresthetica, compressed near the ASIS/inguinal ligament.
cl: burning pain and numbness over the outer front of her right thigh
q.ch: Pregnancy + anterolateral thigh burning + normal motor exam → meralgia paresthetica (lateral femoral cutaneous nerve).
q.tr: Also from tight belts and obesity.
q.q2: Which nerve is entrapped?

q.s: A 68-year-old man taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation has sudden severe right flank and groin pain. His INR is 6.8. He cannot straighten his right knee against gravity, the right knee jerk is absent, and he has numbness over the front of the thigh and inner leg. CT shows a large retroperitoneal hematoma in the iliopsoas.
e: Correct. Quadriceps, patellar reflex, anterior thigh and medial leg (saphenous) sensation.
Wrong. Hamstrings and below the knee.
cl: the right knee jerk is absent
q.ch: Anticoagulant + retroperitoneal hematoma → femoral nerve → weak knee extension, absent patellar reflex.
q.tr: Femoral nerve also compressed by psoas abscess and pelvic fracture.
q.q2: Which nerve is compressed?

q.s: A 31-year-old woman had a prolonged second stage of labor with a large baby. Two weeks later she has leakage of stool and urine and numbness of the perineum.
q.ch: Prolonged labor → pudendal nerve stretch → incontinence + perineal numbness; blocked at the ischial spine.
q.tr: Pudendal = S2, 3, 4 "keeps the poop off the floor."
q.q2: Which bony landmark is used to block this nerve during labor?

q.s: A 45-year-old runner has burning and numbness on the sole of her left foot that worsens with standing. Tapping behind the medial malleolus reproduces the tingling. Plantarflexion strength is normal.
o: Tibial nerve in the tarsal tunnel
e: Correct. Distal tibial nerve lesion; calf muscles are spared.
cl: burning and numbness on the sole
Tinel sign over the tarsal tunnel.
q.ch: Sole paresthesias + Tinel behind medial malleolus + normal calf strength → tarsal tunnel syndrome (distal tibial nerve).
q.tr: Proximal tibial lesion: can't stand on TIPtoes; distal: sole symptoms only.
q.q2: Which nerve is compressed?

q.s: A 19-year-old basketball player lands on another player's foot and rolls his ankle inward. He has swelling and tenderness just in front of the lateral malleolus. He can bear weight with pain.
e: Correct. Most common ankle sprain, from inversion and plantarflexion.
cl: just in front of the lateral malleolus
q.ch: Inversion injury + anterolateral ankle tenderness → ATFL sprain (low ankle sprain).
q.tr: High ankle sprain = AITFL ("high tide").
q.q2: Which ligament is most likely injured?

q.s: A 25-year-old powerlifter attempts a very heavy deadlift. As the tension in his hamstrings and back muscles becomes extreme, the muscles suddenly relax and he drops the bar.
o: Golgi tendon organ; type Ib fibers
e: Correct. Senses tension and inhibits the agonist via an inhibitory interneuron.
cl: the tension in his hamstrings and back muscles becomes extreme
q.ch: Extreme tension → Golgi tendon organ (Ib) → inhibitory interneuron → relaxation of agonist.
q.tr: Spindle = length (contracts); Golgi = tension (relaxes).
q.q2: Which receptor and fiber type mediate this protective reflex?

q.s: A 19-year-old man punched a wall in anger yesterday. He has pain and swelling over the back of his right hand near the little finger, and the knuckle of that finger is depressed.
cl: the knuckle of that finger is depressed
Volar angulation of the metacarpal head.
q.ch: Punching a hard surface → fifth metacarpal neck fracture (boxer's fracture).
q.tr: Boxer's fracture: young men, fifth metacarpal.
q.q2: Which bone is most likely fractured?

q.s: A 48-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes has fever, right flank pain and a tender mass in his right groin. He walks bent forward, and extending his right hip while lying on his left side causes severe pain. CT shows a low-density collection within the right iliopsoas muscle.
e: Wrong. Possible (Pott disease), but not most common.
Correct. Most common cause of psoas abscess.
cl: tender mass in his right groin
extending his right hip while lying on his left side causes severe pain
low-density collection within the right iliopsoas
q.ch: Diabetes + fever + flank/groin pain + psoas sign + CT collection → psoas abscess → S. aureus → drainage and antibiotics.
q.tr: Psoas abscess may also come from vertebral osteomyelitis, pyelonephritis or Crohn disease.
q.q2: Which organism is most likely?

q.s: A 32-year-old woman who recently had a baby has pain on the thumb side of her wrist when lifting her infant. Pain worsens when she tucks her thumb into her fist and bends the wrist toward the little finger.
o: Extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis
Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
e: Correct. De Quervain tenosynovitis; positive Finkelstein test.
cl: pain on the thumb side of her wrist
tucks her thumb into her fist and bends the wrist toward the little finger
q.ch: New mother + radial styloid pain + positive Finkelstein → De Quervain (APL, EPB).
q.tr: Also in golfers, racquet sports and "thumb" texters.
q.q2: Which tendons are affected?

q.s: A 23-year-old man is in the hospital after an open fracture of his tibia was fixed 10 hours ago. He has increasing pain in his lower leg despite morphine. The front of his leg is tense and swollen. Passive stretching of his toes causes severe pain. Dorsalis pedis pulse is palpable. Compartment pressure measurements are shown.
o: Wait for a rise in CK
Elevate the leg above the heart and recheck in 4 hours
e: Correct. Compartment syndrome: delta pressure <30 mmHg.
Wrong. A late sign of irreversible damage.
cl: Long bone fracture is a common cause.
increasing pain in his lower leg despite morphine
Passive stretching of his toes causes severe pain
q.ch: Tibial fracture + pain on passive stretch + tense compartment + delta pressure <30 (table) → compartment syndrome → fasciotomy.
q.tr: Pulselessness and high CK are late; do not wait for them.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

q.s: A 46-year-old overweight teacher has pain on the bottom of her heel that is worst with her first steps out of bed and after sitting, and improves after walking a few minutes. There is tenderness at the medial heel.
e: Correct. Inflammation of the plantar aponeurosis.
cl: worst with her first steps out of bed
q.ch: Overweight + heel pain worst with first steps → plantar fasciitis.
q.tr: Heel spurs often coexist but are not the cause.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 2-year-old girl began crying and stopped using her left arm after her mother pulled her up by the hand to stop her from falling. She holds the arm slightly bent at the elbow with the palm facing down. There is no swelling.
cl: pulled her up by the hand
holds the arm slightly bent at the elbow with the palm facing down
q.ch: Young child + sudden arm pull + flexed pronated arm, no swelling → radial head subluxation (annular ligament).
q.tr: Reduce with supination–flexion or hyperpronation.
q.q2: Which structure has slipped over the radial head?

q.s: A 13-year-old soccer player has pain and a tender bony prominence just below his right kneecap. Pain worsens with running, jumping and kneeling. He grew 8 cm in the past year.
o: Repetitive traction and avulsion at the tibial tuberosity ossification center
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head
cl: tender bony prominence just below his right kneecap
He grew 8 cm in the past year
q.ch: Adolescent athlete after growth spurt + painful tibial tuberosity → Osgood-Schlatter (traction apophysitis).
q.tr: Osgood-Schlatter = tibial tuberosity.
q.q2: What is the underlying cause?

q.s: A newborn girl delivered in breech position has a "clunk" when her hip is flexed, abducted and lifted forward during examination. Her mother asks for an x-ray.
e: Wrong. The femoral head is not ossified until about 4–6 months.
Correct. Developmental dysplasia of the hip.
q.ch: Breech girl + Ortolani clunk → DDH → ultrasound (cartilage not ossified).
q.tr: Barlow dislocates; Ortolani relocates.
q.q2: Which imaging study is most appropriate?

q.s: A 7-year-old boy fell onto his outstretched hand. He has tenderness over the distal radius. X-ray shows a bulging of the bony cortex on one side of the distal radius without a visible fracture line extending across the bone.
o: Torus (buckle) fracture from axial compression with an intact tension side
Pathologic fracture from a bone cyst
Greenstick fracture failing on the tension side
cl: without a visible fracture line extending across the bone
q.ch: Child + axial load + cortical buckle without full fracture → torus fracture.
q.tr: Greenstick bends like a twig; torus buckles like a can.
q.q2: Which of the following best describes this injury?

q.s: A 40-year-old woman with fatigue, cough and red tender nodules on her shins has bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest x-ray. She has also developed kidney stones and confusion. Her laboratory results are shown.
o: Macrophages in granulomas converting vitamin D to its active form
e: Correct. Hypervitaminosis D from sarcoidosis: high Ca and PO4, suppressed PTH.
cl: red tender nodules on her shins
q.ch: Sarcoidosis + high Ca and PO4 + suppressed PTH + high calcitriol (table) → granulomatous 1α-hydroxylase activity → hypervitaminosis D.
q.tr: High Ca with low PTH means the cause is outside the parathyroid.
q.q2: Which of the following best explains her hypercalcemia?

q.s: A 17-year-old boy has a dull ache in his left thigh for 4 months that is worse at night and dramatically relieved by ibuprofen. X-ray shows a 1-cm round lucency surrounded by dense sclerotic bone in the femoral cortex.
e: Correct. Osteoid osteoma; NSAIDs block prostaglandin synthesis.
cl: 1-cm round lucency surrounded by dense sclerotic bone
q.ch: Young male + night pain relieved by NSAIDs + small cortical nidus → osteoid osteoma → prostaglandins.
q.tr: Osteoid osteoma: <1.5 cm, NSAIDs work; osteoblastoma: >2 cm, spine, NSAIDs don't work.
q.q2: Which mediator is responsible for his pain pattern?

q.s: A 64-year-old man has deep, progressive pain in his right hip for 6 months. CT shows a lytic lesion in the medulla of the proximal femur with ring-and-arc calcifications, scalloping of the inner cortex and a break through the cortex.
e: Correct. Chondrosarcoma, most common in adults >50 in the pelvis, proximal femur and humerus.
q.ch: Older adult + medullary lytic lesion with calcifications + endosteal erosion → chondrosarcoma.
q.tr: Chondrosarcoma = older adults, central skeleton.
q.q2: Which cell type makes up this tumor?

q.s: A 67-year-old woman has pain in her fingers and right knee that is worse at the end of the day and improves with rest. Morning stiffness lasts 10 minutes. She has bony swellings at the distal and proximal interphalangeal joints. Her knee aspirate and x-ray findings are shown.
e: Correct. Osteoarthritis: mechanical stress destroys cartilage, with inadequate chondrocyte-mediated repair.
cl: worse at the end of the day and improves with rest
bony swellings at the distal and proximal interphalangeal joints
q.ch: Older woman + mechanical pain + Heberden/Bouchard nodes + noninflammatory fluid + osteophytes (table) → osteoarthritis → chondrocyte-mediated inadequate repair.
q.tr: OA: DIP involved; RA: DIP spared.
q.q2: Which cell type plays the main role in the inadequate repair of this disease?

head: Finding
Result
rows: Asymmetric joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and cysts

q.s: A 52-year-old man has an acutely swollen, painful right knee. X-ray shows linear calcification within the cartilage. Joint fluid has rhomboid crystals that are blue when parallel to the compensator. He also has diabetes, darkening skin and erectile dysfunction.
e: Correct. CPPD deposition associated with hemochromatosis.
cl: rhomboid crystals that are blue when parallel
diabetes, darkening skin and erectile dysfunction
q.ch: CPPD (chondrocalcinosis, rhomboid positive crystals) + features of iron overload → hemochromatosis → iron studies.
q.tr: CPPD associations: hemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism, joint trauma.
q.q2: Which test would best identify the associated condition?

q.s: A 50-year-old woman has a gritty feeling in her eyes and needs to sip water to swallow dry food. Her teeth have multiple cavities. Both parotid glands are enlarged. Her laboratory results are shown.
e: Correct. Sjögren syndrome increases the risk of B-cell lymphoma.
cl: needs to sip water to swallow dry food
q.ch: Dry eyes + dry mouth + caries + anti-SSA/SSB + lymphocytic sialadenitis (table) → Sjögren → MALT lymphoma risk.
q.tr: Sjögren: lacrimal and salivary destruction; RF can be positive without RA.
q.q2: Two years later her left parotid gland enlarges rapidly. Which complication should be suspected?

q.s: An 8-year-old boy with sickle cell disease has fever and severe pain in his right tibia for 5 days. The leg is warm, red and swollen. MRI shows marrow edema and a subperiosteal fluid collection in the metaphysis.
e: Wrong. Septic arthritis in young adults.
Correct. Osteomyelitis in sickle cell disease (S. aureus remains common overall).
cl: fever and severe pain in his right tibia
q.ch: Sickle cell disease + hematogenous metaphyseal osteomyelitis → Salmonella.
q.tr: Puncture wound → Pseudomonas; prosthesis → S. epidermidis; sickle cell → Salmonella.
q.q2: Which organism is classically associated with this infection in patients with sickle cell disease?

q.s: A 45-year-old man with scaly plaques on his elbows has a painful, swollen left middle finger along its whole length and swelling of the right second toe. His fingernails have small pits. X-ray of a DIP joint shows erosion that makes one bone end look like a pencil sitting in a cup.
e: Correct. Dactylitis, nail pitting, pencil-in-cup deformity.
Wrong. Not with psoriasis and nail pits.
cl: swollen left middle finger along its whole length
q.ch: Psoriasis + asymmetric dactylitis + nail pitting + pencil-in-cup DIP erosion → psoriatic arthritis.
q.tr: Seronegative spondyloarthritis = PAIR, HLA-B27.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 6-year-old girl has had fevers to 39.8°C every evening for 3 weeks that return to normal by morning. During the fevers she has a faint, salmon-pink rash on her trunk that disappears when the fever breaks. Both knees and wrists are swollen. She has leukocytosis, thrombocytosis and a high ESR. Blood cultures are negative.
cl: fevers to 39.8°C every evening for 3 weeks
salmon-pink rash on her trunk that disappears when the fever breaks
Both knees and wrists are swollen
q.ch: Child + quotidian fever + evanescent salmon rash + polyarthritis + inflammatory labs → systemic JIA → uveitis screening.
q.tr: Systemic JIA: quotidian fever + evanescent salmon rash + arthritis.
q.q2: Which eye complication requires regular screening?

q.s: A 38-year-old woman has 2 years of widespread aching in her neck, shoulders, back and hips, unrefreshing sleep, fatigue and trouble concentrating. Pressing on several points causes marked tenderness. Strength, joints, ESR, CRP, CK and TSH are normal.
o: Regular aerobic exercise and an SNRI, TCA or gabapentinoid
cl: unrefreshing sleep, fatigue and trouble concentrating
Pressing on several points causes marked tenderness
ESR, CRP, CK and TSH are normal
q.ch: Young/middle-aged woman + widespread pain + tender points + sleep/cognitive symptoms + normal labs → fibromyalgia → exercise + SNRI/TCA/gabapentinoid.
q.tr: Normal inflammatory markers separate fibromyalgia from PMR.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

q.s: A 60-year-old man has back pain and rising creatinine. CT shows a dense rind of soft tissue around the abdominal aorta that pulls both ureters toward the midline, with bilateral hydronephrosis. He was previously diagnosed with autoimmune pancreatitis. Biopsy shows dense fibrosis with many plasma cells.
e: Correct. IgG4-related disease (retroperitoneal fibrosis and autoimmune pancreatitis).
cl: dense rind of soft tissue around the abdominal aorta
dense fibrosis with many plasma cells
q.ch: Retroperitoneal fibrosis + autoimmune pancreatitis + plasma cell–rich fibrosis → IgG4-related disease.
q.tr: IgG4 disease: salivary/lacrimal glands, Riedel thyroiditis, pancreas, aorta, retroperitoneum.
q.q2: Which serum finding is most likely?

q.s: A 27-year-old woman from Korea has had fever, night sweats, joint aches and pain in her arms when she uses them. Her blood pressure readings are shown. Bruits are heard over both subclavian arteries. ESR is 78 mm/h.
e: Wrong. Arms would be higher than legs.
Correct. "Pulseless disease": granulomatous narrowing of the aortic arch and its branches.
cl: pain in her arms when she uses them
Bruits are heard over both subclavian arteries
q.ch: Young Asian woman + constitutional symptoms + arm claudication + low, unequal arm BP with higher leg BP (table) → Takayasu arteritis.
q.tr: Takayasu = young Asian women; GCA = older women.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 50-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B has fever, weight loss, abdominal pain after meals, new hypertension and sudden right foot drop. Urinalysis shows mild proteinuria without red cell casts. Mesenteric angiography shows multiple small aneurysms.
e: Correct. Polyarteritis nodosa spares the lungs.
cl: 30% of PAN patients are HBsAg positive.
q.ch: Hepatitis B + systemic symptoms + mesenteric ischemia + mononeuritis + microaneurysms → PAN → lungs spared.
q.tr: PAN affects the SKIN: Skin, Kidneys, Intestines, Nerves.
q.q2: Which organ is typically NOT involved in this disease?

q.s: A 34-year-old man who smokes two packs of cigarettes daily has painful, bluish fingertips with a small ulcer on his left index finger. He has had painful, tender cords along veins in his legs. Pulses at both wrists and ankles are reduced.
cl: smokes two packs of cigarettes daily
painful, bluish fingertips with a small ulcer
tender cords along veins in his legs
q.ch: Young heavy smoker + digital ischemia + migratory phlebitis + distal pulse loss → Buerger disease → stop smoking.
q.tr: Buerger involves arteries, veins and nerves (segmental thrombosing vasculitis).
q.q2: Which intervention is most important?

q.s: A 7-year-old boy has raised purple spots on his buttocks and legs, pain in his knees and ankles, and crampy abdominal pain. He had a cold 2 weeks ago. Platelet count is normal. Urinalysis shows red cells.
cl: raised purple spots on his buttocks and legs
pain in his knees and ankles
He had a cold 2 weeks ago
q.ch: Child after URI + palpable purpura with normal platelets + arthralgia + abdominal pain + hematuria → IgA vasculitis → intussusception risk.
q.tr: IgA vasculitis is associated with IgA nephropathy.
q.q2: Which abdominal complication should be monitored for?

q.s: A 30-year-old man of Turkish descent has had repeated painful mouth ulcers and genital ulcers. He now has blurred vision from inflammation inside the eye and painful red nodules on his shins. A small papule developed at a needle-stick site.
cl: repeated painful mouth ulcers and genital ulcers
painful red nodules on his shins
q.ch: Turkish ancestry + oral and genital ulcers + uveitis + erythema nodosum → Behçet → HLA-B51.
q.tr: Behçet is a variable-vessel vasculitis.
q.q2: Which HLA type is associated with this condition?

q.s: A 28-year-old woman has drooping eyelids and double vision that worsen through the day, and difficulty chewing by the end of meals. Reflexes are normal. Results of low-frequency repetitive nerve stimulation are shown.
o: Chest CT for small cell lung cancer
e: Correct. Myasthenia gravis: decremental response; associated with thymoma and thymic hyperplasia.
cl: drooping eyelids and double vision that worsen through the day
difficulty chewing by the end of meals
q.ch: Fatigable ocular and bulbar weakness + normal reflexes + decremental CMAP (figure) → myasthenia gravis (anti-AChR) → look for thymoma.
q.tr: Myasthenia worsens with use; treat with pyridostigmine.
q.q2: Which imaging study should be performed?
q.fc: Compound muscle action potential during repetitive stimulation

q.s: A 42-year-old woman with tight, shiny skin of her fingers, forearms, face and trunk that progressed over 8 months suddenly develops headache and blurred vision. Blood pressure is 210/124 mmHg. Creatinine has risen from 0.8 to 2.6 mg/dL. Smear shows schistocytes.
e: Correct. Scleroderma renal crisis in diffuse systemic sclerosis.
cl: tight, shiny skin of her fingers, forearms, face and trunk
Creatinine has risen from 0.8 to 2.6 mg/dL
q.ch: Diffuse systemic sclerosis + malignant hypertension + AKI + MAHA → scleroderma renal crisis → ACE inhibitor.
q.tr: Diffuse scleroderma: anti-Scl-70 and anti-RNA polymerase III (renal crisis risk).
q.q2: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

q.s: A 3-week-old infant has fever and a red rash that began around the mouth and spread over the body within a day. The top layer of skin peels off in large sheets with gentle pressure, leaving moist, red skin. The lips, mouth and eyes are not involved.
o: Between keratinocytes in the stratum spinosum by autoantibodies
Stratum granulosum, from a bacterial exotoxin
cl: peels off in large sheets with gentle pressure
The lips, mouth and eyes are not involved
q.ch: Newborn + fever + Nikolsky-positive superficial sloughing without mucosal involvement → SSSS → exfoliative toxin splits stratum granulosum.
q.tr: SSSS spares the mucosa and heals completely; TEN involves mucosa.
q.q2: Where in the skin does the separation occur?

q.s: An 82-year-old man in a nursing home has had itchy hives on his trunk and thighs for weeks, which have now formed large, firm, fluid-filled blisters that do not rupture easily. His mouth is normal. Rubbing normal skin does not cause peeling.
o: Subepidermal blister with eosinophils and linear IgG/C3 at the basement membrane
IgA deposits at dermal papillae tips
Intraepidermal acantholysis with a "row of tombstones"
cl: large, firm, fluid-filled blisters that do not rupture easily
Rubbing normal skin does not cause peeling
q.ch: Older adult + urticarial prodrome + tense bullae + no mucosal involvement + Nikolsky negative → bullous pemphigoid → subepidermal blister, linear IgG.
q.tr: Hemidesmosomes are "bullow" — bullous pemphigoid.
q.q2: Biopsy would most likely show which finding?

q.s: Two patients have ulcers on the lower leg. Their findings are shown; patient 1 stands all day at work.
o: Has a neuropathic ulcer from diabetes
Has peripheral artery disease and needs revascularization
Has a venous ulcer from chronic venous insufficiency, the most common ulcer type
e: Wrong. SCC in a chronic scar.
cl: Two patients have ulcers on the lower leg
Location, appearance, pain and pulses distinguish them.
patient 1 stands all day at work
q.ch: Patient 1: gaiter area, shallow, edema, varicosities, normal pulses (table) → venous ulcer. Patient 2: distal, punched out, painful, no pulses → arterial ulcer.
q.tr: Venous pain eases with elevation; arterial pain worsens with elevation.
q.q2: Which statement about patient 1 is correct?
